title: Linear night fits leave a 3.20 m/s GJ 191 extraction difference in 32 HARPS exposures from 2021
abstract: We test whether linear drift within each night explains a known GJ 191 velocity difference between DRS and SERVAL. Eight nights in HARPS-RVBank version 02 contain four exposures each in about half an hour. Free night offsets and slopes leave a 3.198 m/s difference RMS and Q = 99.818 for 16 residual degrees of freedom. We use the sum of the two quoted errors as a maximum difference error. The conditional independent Gaussian tail is 3.75e-14. A conservative bound that allows arbitrary Gaussian correlation within each night is 0.020, if nights are independent. Removal of one night retains excess scatter under the independent error model. A quadratic night model leaves 2.625 m/s RMS, but the general correlation bound does not reject it. The target and subset were selected after inspection. The cause is not known. No planet or independent telescope confirmation is reported. Original code, aggregate evidence, a noise bound, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included. External database records are excluded.

display.caption: Residual error scores after separate polynomial night fits. Difference errors use the sum of quoted reduction errors. Individual products use their own quoted errors. Earlier and 2021 samples have different observing windows.

citations.reason: This short-pair result motivates our new test that removes a separate polynomial drift from each night.
